title: Jay-Z Brings His ‘Jay-Z 30’ Concert Series to a Close in Los Angeles With Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short
description: How does one measure their own legacy: In a series of shows, in the decades since a debut album, in an exhaustive eight-part docuseries breaking do
body:
How does one measure their own legacy: In a series of shows, in the decades since a debut album, in an exhaustive eight-part docuseries breaking down the intricacies of rhymes laid down years ago? That seemed to be the existential question looming over “Jay-Z 30,” a yearlong celebration that began with a spectacular one-off headlining performance at the Roots Picnic in late May and concluded on Saturday night with the second of two shows at Inglewood, California’s SoFi Stadium.
	

	For Jay, legacy has clearly been weighing on his mind. A new generation of hip-hop artists has emerged, and the decade-long gap since he released an album has opened a space for that generation to question his legacy. So it made sense that he’d revisit his catalog brick by brick, show by show, celebrating a career-long work in progress that crescendoed to a global tour after nearly a decade of artistic dormancy. At SoFi, much like his previous concerts, his performance was a reminder — no, a reinforcement — that nothing at that scale is by accident. And he said as much as the curtain fell on an hour-and-a-half finale of his “Jay-Z 30” series, encouraging those in attendance to believe in what they’ve actually witnessed.


	“You gotta be really real with what’s going on in the world,” he said during closer “Encore.” It was a direct rebuttal to the rash of tweets and social media posts claiming that SoFi wasn’t entirely sold out, or that many of the tickets had been given away. “People will tell you that nobody was in here tonight, but you got eyes. You can see. People will tell you that the music wasn’t great, but you got ears. You gotta understand, you gotta question everything. This world with AI and everything, it’s been going on forever. They called it propaganda before. But now, the technology has caught up and people are tricked. A lot of tricknology for us… Make sure you question everything you feel.”
	


	Jay makes that music that you can feel. That’s been the thrill of his shows over the past five months. For those who experienced his rise in real time (and, frankly, many at SoFi probably had, based on their millennial look), Jay has been a pop impresario, a cultural touchstone who helped graft hip-hop culture onto the mainstream. He’s done it through a breathless string of number one albums and hits, and in boardrooms and closed-door meetings. “Jay-Z 30” was an invitation to revisit the path that he took to get there, a way to show that legacy isn’t about the hit that’s next, but rather the ones you landed to get there.

	Much like his other performances, the setlist at Jay’s final night at SoFi was somewhat static — “Girls, Girls, Girls,” for instance, once again bled into “’03 Bonnie & Clyde,” while “N—s in Paris” delightfully mashed into “Big Pimpin’.” But the finer details are what make a Jay show such an experience. At each of his shows, he’s found a way to pay homage to the city that’s welcomed him. In Philadelphia, that included guest appearances from Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal and his Roc-A-Fella crew, including Freeway, Beanie Sigel and Peedi Crakk. In New York City, throughout his three-night run at Yankee Stadium, he brought out Alicia Keys for “Empire State of Mind,” as well as Fat Joe and Jadakiss. Naturally, a narrative emerged: Can he really perform a solid headlining set without a supporting cast to sweeten the deal?

	Perhaps that’s why the guest count at his SoFi shows was so thin compared to others. On Saturday night, he tapped Too Short to perform “Blow the Whistle,” shouting out the Bay Area. Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg came out to do a medley of their own massive hits, including “Nuthin’ But a ‘G’ Thang” and “Still D.R.E.” But it was mainly Jay, every day, in all his resplendence. He traipsed from era to era, hit to hit, his breath control and spark as refined as ever. This was performance at its peak, a marvel to behold of an artist who helped build hip-hop as an institution while adding to the story still being written.


	As for what’s next? Rumors have swirled about a new album from collaborators who quickly backpedaled on their statements. The looming question mark of a Super Bowl Halftime Show performance hung in the air at SoFi on Saturday night. But for a string of concerts and a few activations here and there, it felt only right that Jay-Z justify the experience while rapping “Heart of the City (Ain’t No Love)” near the end of the show: “Jigga held you down 30 summers, damn, where’s the love?”

(Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg)99 ProblemsGirls, Girls, GirlsExcuse Me MissLa-La-La (Excuse Me Miss Again)Change the GameI Just Wanna Love U (Give It 2 Me)Money, Cash, HoesJigga My N—aHeart of the City (Ain’t No Love)Empire State of MindN—s in Paris / Big Pimpin’Public Service Announcement (Interlude)Encore

title: Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Forza,” Marco Balsamo’s soccer drama shot between Bali and Milan, has been picked up for international sales by EST N8, which will take the film t
body:
“Forza,” Marco Balsamo’s soccer drama shot between Bali and Milan, has been picked up for international sales by EST N8, which will take the film to the Tokyo International Film Festival‘s TIFFCOM market (Oct. 28–30). Before that, it gets its first public screening on Oct. 25 at Jakarta Film Week.

	Balsamo’s first feature as director centers on Bima, an 11-year-old from Bali who hopes a career as a pro footballer will give his family a better life. A chance bond with a former AC Milan player in the last stretch of his career changes the outlook for both of them.
	

	Newcomer Ghazi Alhabsyi heads the cast. Balsamo also appears on screen, alongside Tara Sibel Demren, AC Milan icon Alessandro Costacurta and Atiqah Hasiholan, Oka Antara and Tio Pakusadewo, all three winners at the Indonesian Film Festival (FFI).


	Balsamo wrote the script and produced with Demren. Riva Studios originated the project, and its producers include Ario Sagantoro of “The Raid” franchise. Adhya Pictures has the film’s Indonesian theatrical release, set for 2027.

	Interest at home is strong. Both rounds of online tickets for the Jakarta screening, at CGV Grand Indonesia, sold out inside five minutes.

	“‘Forza’ follows a boy from Bali and a former pro footballer who open new doors for each other, and it bridges Indonesia and Italy the way only football can,” said Sophie Shi, head of studios at EST N8. “It’s a film for audiences around the world, with a story of family and hope that transcends language and culture. Our mission is to take bold Asian stories to audiences worldwide, and a family film told through the world’s most popular sport is built to travel. We’re proud to launch ‘Forza’ to buyers at TIFFCOM.”
	

	Shi and Jan Paul Villanueva negotiated the deal for EST N8, with Balsamo and Demren representing Riva Studios. Villanueva, EVP of acquisitions and global distribution, will lead sales with Cathy Ni, head of sales and U.S. distribution, and Shams Pasha, global sales and marketing executive.

	“We’ve spent years bringing ‘Forza’ to the screen, and Indonesia has been at the heart of it from the beginning,” Balsamo said. “This film is a labor of love and a testament to the perseverance and collaboration behind independent filmmaking. Sharing the film at Jakarta Film Week is especially meaningful. It’s a moment we’ve been looking forward to for a long time.”

	Demren, who co-founded Riva Studios, said the film was designed for families to watch side by side and discuss afterward. “We hope Bima’s journey reminds audiences how much it matters to have someone believe in you, especially when your dreams feel out of reach,” she said. “Seeing both ticket releases fill so quickly is an encouraging start. We’re looking forward to hearing audiences’ reactions.”

	Demren and Balsamo set up Riva Studios in 2022 as an independent outfit working in live action, animation and music. In 2024 it bought French animation house TeamTO. “Forza” is its first live-action feature.

	Also on EST N8’s TIFFCOM lineup are “Tame,” a Thai horror title from B-EST Pictures; Dean Colin Marcial’s crime thriller “Jaguar,” set in Manila; “Master,” Rezwan Shahriar Sumit’s winner of IFFR’s Big Screen Award; “Pilgrims,” a Korean sci-fi animation from Heo Pyoungkang that was selected for Annecy; and “The Invisible Half,” a J-horror from Nishiyama Masaki.

	The company, which brought together EST Studios and N8, has offices in Los Angeles and Bangkok and has sold and distributed more than 60 titles across over 100 territories. Its catalog includes “Hidden Letters,” which was shortlisted for the Oscars and nominated for an Emmy; “The Monk and the Gun,” Bhutan’s Oscar entry; “A Useful Ghost,” which won the Grand Prize at Cannes Critics’ Week; and “Blood Brothers,” which topped Netflix’s global chart.

title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2
description: Stars of “Squid Game” and “KPop Demon Hunters” took the stage in Seoul on Oct. 24 as Netflix celebrated 10 years in Korea with a fan festival, wher
body:
Stars of “Squid Game” and “KPop Demon Hunters” took the stage in Seoul on Oct. 24 as Netflix celebrated 10 years in Korea with a fan festival, where co-CEO Ted Sarandos previewed upcoming titles including “Tantara” and “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2.

	“Squid Game” was represented by Lee Jung-jae, Lee Byung-hun and Park Hae-soo, while Ahn Hyo-seop appeared for “KPop Demon Hunters.” Also on stage were Koo Kyo-hwan and Jung Hae-in of “D.P.,” Kim Hyun-joo of “Hellbound,” Yum Hye-ran of “Mask Girl” and Lee Se-dol of “The Devil’s Plan,” among others.
	

	Dubbed “Netflix Janchi,” the two-day event ran Oct. 24-25 at Sangam Oil Tank Culture Park. Thousands of fans turned out for themed booths, games, merchandise and live music.


	“Ten years ago, we dreamed big. But none of us could have imagined that Korean stories would move hearts around the world, and land right at the center of global culture,” Sarandos said.

	Of the new titles, Lee Chang-dong’s Venice winner “Possible Love,” headlined by Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong and Jo In-sung, bows Nov. 6. “Tantara,” starring Song Hye-kyo, Gong Yoo and Kim Seol-hyun, follows on Dec. 11. Still undated are “Grand Galaxy Hotel,” with Lee Do-hyun and Shin Si-a; “She, Wolf,” previously known by the working title “Beauty in the Beast,” with Kim Min-ju, Lomon and Moon Sang-min; “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2, with Park Ji-hu, Yoon Chan-young, Cho Yi-hyun and Lomon; and “Solo Leveling,” with Byeon Woo-seok.

	Netflix launched in Korea on Jan. 6, 2016. Its first international film was Bong Joon Ho’s “Okja.” The first Korean original, the stand-up special “Yoo Byung Jae: Too Much Information,” arrived in March 2018, and “Kingdom” became its first Korean series in January 2019. In July 2021, “Kingdom: Ashin of the North” became the first Korean show to crack the Global Top 10, charting in 58 countries.
	

	Netflix has counted upward of 200 Korean titles on its Global Top 10 since it began compiling the chart in June 2021. “Squid Game” Season 1 holds the record for the longest run at 32 straight weeks, nine of them at No. 1. The show’s three seasons are the streamer’s three most-watched non-English series ever, and “Teach You a Lesson” now ranks No. 10 on that list, making it Netflix’s biggest Korean show after “Squid Game.” No other non-English content draws more viewing on Netflix than K-content, and over four in five of its subscribers worldwide have sampled at least one Korean title.

	“For Netflix, Korea is more than a market. It is where we discovered new possibilities, and where we learned how far a story can travel. And it is one of our most treasured partners for the future we are building together,” Sarandos said.

	Between 2024 and 2026, first-time directors or writers made more than a third of Netflix’s Korean titles. Park Yoon-seo, an assistant director on “Kingdom” Season 2, made his directing debut this year with YA horror series “If Wishes Could Kill.”

	“Netflix gave me an opportunity when I was an assistant director on ‘Kingdom: Season 2.’ I’m glad I was able to give new actors that same opportunity,” Park said. He added that he had suggested casting only newcomers to keep the series fresh, and that Netflix signed off because fame wasn’t the priority.

	Baek Seung-min was a second lighting assistant on “Kingdom” and now heads lighting on “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2. “Working with Netflix Korea at important stages of my career has helped me grow professionally,” he said.

	From 2016 to 2025, Netflix partnered with more than 80 Korean production companies on shows employing upward of 20,000 actors and crew members, along with 70,000 extras and day workers. Shoots took place in more than 100 cities and towns, with over half outside the Seoul Capital Area in locations such as Busan, Jeonju and Jeju. “When Life Gives You Tangerines” alone drew on nearly 4,000 suppliers and a cast and crew of 600, adding more than KRW90 billion ($60.4 million) to the Korean economy. Netflix’s skills and training programs reached over 6,500 people in Korea between 2021 and 2025.

	To get those shows to viewers abroad, Netflix now relies on 122 localization partners globally, 119 of them dubbing studios.
	

	Colorist Park Jin-young, whose credits include “Possible Love” and “Good News,” said Netflix’s arrival in Korea came just as HDR technology was going commercial. “It felt like going from working with 30 colors of paint for 10 or 20 years to suddenly having 100 colors at my disposal,” he said.

	Unscripted formats have also exported well. “Physical: 100” became the first unscripted show not in English to lead the Global Top 10, and local versions have followed in Italy and Mexico, with U.S., French and Swedish editions on the way.

	The streamer also pointed to effects off screen. According to Netflix, 72% of subscribers who watch K-content have said they’d like to travel to Korea. Jeju drew about 2.24 million overseas visitors in 2025, its most in nine years, coinciding with the premiere of “When Life Gives You Tangerines,” while visits to the show’s Gimnyeong Beach location jumped about 96%. Chef Choi Hyun-seok’s restaurant Choi saw sales rise 300% after “Culinary Class Wars” Season 1, and bookings at restaurants of Season 2 contestants climbed 303%.

	In the U.S., new Korean learners on Duolingo rose 37% in the week “Squid Game” Season 3 launched. Applications for Korea’s TOPIK language exam passed 550,000 in September 2025, three months on from “KPop Demon Hunters,” beating the total for all of 2024. Between April 2025 and March 2026, K-content logged more than 12 billion viewing hours on Netflix, behind only U.S. productions, and rights to the “Hellbound” webtoon have sold to 11 countries since the series launched.

	Netflix has also opened a Korean-language microsite charting the people, locations and numbers behind its first decade in the country.

schema.headline: ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2

title: SAG-AFTRA Extends Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract and Adds CEO to Title
description: The SAG-AFTRA board voted Saturday to extend the contract of Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, the union’s national executive director, for four years and t
body:
The SAG-AFTRA board voted Saturday to extend the contract of Duncan Crabtree-Ireland, the union’s national executive director, for four years and to add CEO to his title.

	Crabtree-Ireland’s contract was set to expire in 2028, but will now run through June 20, 2032. The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed. He was paid $1.1 million for the 2026 fiscal year.

	The extension will carry Crabtree-Ireland through the next round of negotiations with the major studios, with the current deal set to expire in June 2030. In a statement, the union said that the extension will offer “added stability and continuity for the union during a time of unprecedented industry disruption.”
	

	Crabtree-Ireland has spent nearly his entire career at SAG-AFTRA, serving as general counsel and chief operating officer before being named national executive director in 2021. He has made artificial intelligence a key focus of the union’s negotiations, reaching a series of agreements that aim to allow performers to capture the upside of AI while protecting them from unauthorized uses of their likenesses. He was also a central figure in the 2023 actors’ strike.


	Sean Astin, the president of SAG-AFTRA, praised Crabtree-Ireland in a statement after the vote.

	“To battle giant global transnational corporations, we need expert leadership with a track record of successful bargaining and significant operational management expertise,” Astin said. “That is Duncan. He is a powerful executive who has led our union at the bargaining table, in the halls of Congress and in boardrooms and conference rooms across the industry and the world. We are thrilled to have guaranteed Duncan’s continued service to the members of SAG-AFTRA.”
	

	The extension was approved with 98.34% of the board in favor in a weighted vote.

	“Leading SAG-AFTRA’s staff is the honor of my career, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to keep doing this work,” Crabtree-Ireland said. “As we continue fighting for human creativity, the coming years will be crucial for charting the path forward. I intend to fight alongside our leadership to make sure our members control their image, likeness, voice, and destiny in the workplace, and that they are compensated fairly in the process. I thank President Astin, the national officers, and the National Board for their trust, and our extraordinary staff team for everything they make possible.”

	Pictured: Duncan Crabtree-Ireland (left) and SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin.

schema.headline: SAG-AFTRA Extends Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract and Adds CEO to Title

title: AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The AI technology behind Star Plus and JioHotstar series “Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh” is headed to Indonesia. There, its developer Galleri5 and fell
body:
The AI technology behind Star Plus and JioHotstar series “Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh” is headed to Indonesia. There, its developer Galleri5 and fellow Collective company Collective Studios’ Historyverse plan to create film and series properties drawn from the country’s myths and history.

	Historyverse, which handles original IP and studio work for Collective Artists Network, is partnering with Galleri5 and Singhasari Special Economic Zone on the venture. Projects will cover mythology, fantasy, history and animation. Indonesian creatives and cultural specialists will work alongside Historyverse’s IP development team, using production tools Galleri5 built in India.
	

	The first project being discussed is “Echoes of Nusantara,” a working title for an original mythology-adventure. Historyverse will run creative development, production and IP packaging, and will collaborate with local talent to get projects ready for possible financing, production and distribution outside Indonesia.


	“The next global entertainment franchises will not all come from Hollywood,” said Vijay Subramaniam, founder and group CEO of Collective Artists Network. “Every market has stories that deserve to travel further, and Indonesia has an extraordinary wealth of them. Our ambition with Collective Studios’ Historyverse is to work with Indonesian creators to develop these stories into films, series and larger entertainment properties for the world. Galleri5 gives us a new way to approach the scale of filmmaking, while the creative vision and the stories themselves remain at the center.”
	

	Galleri5’s main product, G5 AI Studio, brings more than 200 AI models together with purpose-built tools for storyboarding, designing characters and worlds, animation, VFX and film-quality video. More than 10,000 ads and videos have been made on the platform. JioStar and Collective Media Network launched “Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh,” and Galleri5 built and ran the AI filmmaking technology behind the show. The company is now developing workflows for Historyverse’s theatrical slate, which includes “Chiranjeevi Hanuman – The Eternal” and “Krishna.” Those productions give Galleri5 a base for refining its technology against real-world creative and production demands.

	“The next generation of global cinema will be built on a very different technology foundation,” said Rahul Regulapati, founder and CEO of Galleri5 and a partner at Collective Artists Network. “At Galleri5, we’re building that foundation with G5 AI Studio, bringing frontier AI models and filmmaking workflows into one platform. We’ve already demonstrated what this technology can do through films and television in India. Now, together with Indonesia’s extraordinary creative talent and Collective’s studio capabilities, we have an opportunity to take locally rooted stories to audiences around the world.”

	For Indonesian creators, the partnership is a chance to match stories led by local talent, and their own original IP, with tools meant to scale up production.

	Airlangga Hartarto, Indonesia’s coordinating minister for economic affairs and chairman of the National Council for Special Economic Zones, said the country had no plans to sit on the sidelines of AI development or simply act as a consumer of the technology. “We intend to help shape it. Special Economic Zones allow us to turn that ambition into real productivity, skilled jobs for our young people and new sources of growth on the path to 8 percent,” he said.

	Singhasari will introduce the venture to Indonesian creators, studios, investors, distributors and creative-economy institutions, and help set up local partnerships and routes to market.

	KRAT David Santoso KR, CEO of Lokanima and Singhasari Special Economic Zone, said the Kingdom of Singhasari had flourished eight centuries ago on the land the zone now occupies. It was a hub for engineering, the arts, scholarship and government, and its culture was enriched by hundreds of years of contact with India. “Today, with our partners from India, we are bringing that history back to life, this time by mastering the AI transformation. Our aim is to build new competitiveness for Indonesia in the new-technology and digital-content subsectors, with Indonesian talent and IP at its heart,” he said.
	

	India’s ambassador to Indonesia, Sandeep Chakravorty, said the Ramayana and the Mahabharata had been part of Indonesian temple culture, wayang (traditional puppet theater) and the popular imagination for over a millennium. “Today, India and Indonesia are writing the next chapter of that shared story with artificial intelligence,” he said.

schema.headline: AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Nathan Fielder Negotiated a ‘Kill Switch’ on ‘You Can See Everything,’ Says Lance Oppenheim: ‘If We Didn’t Find Something, We Could Just Throw It All Away’
description: “You Can See Everything” might be the buzziest film of the moment, but before the Elizabeth Holmes-focused documentary made it to theaters, co-dire
body:
“You Can See Everything” might be the buzziest film of the moment, but before the Elizabeth Holmes-focused documentary made it to theaters, co-director Lance Oppenheim has admitted that fellow director Nathan Fielder was so skeptical about being able to weave a unique enough narrative that he negotiated a “kill switch” with A24 before they began filming.

	In an interview with IndieWire, Oppenheim detailed Fielder’s kill-switch idea and how it helped the project. While Fielder wanted to pursue the documentary with Oppenheim, he worried that “the story had been told so many times already.” (Before the documentary even began production, Holmes’ scandal was already the subject of a popular podcast, best-selling book, an Alex Gibney doc and “The Dropout,” the Hulu scripted series.)
	

	“Nathan [said to A24], ‘Well, do you think if Lance and I were to go and see if there was something there, would you be comfortable with giving us money and essentially just leaving us alone, and giving us a provision in our deal, whatever the money was, that we could just kill it at any time? If we didn’t find something, we could just throw it all away, we could throw it in the garbage can,’” said Oppenheim. “And they thankfully agreed.”


	Oppenheim continued, saying that the “kill switch” negotiation “changed everything,” especially as Fielder remained hesitant about how the doc would come to fruition with just 34 days left before Holmes was set to go to prison. The provision also gave them freedom with the project, he said.

	“This was the first time where I’ve ever been like, ‘Oh, we actually have room to explore something without any pressure of anyone looking [over us],” said Oppenheim. “ I wish I could have that for every project, because then it really feels like you’re just operating purely out of curiosity. You can essentially fish.”
	

	In another interview with Wired Magazine, Fielder also touched on why he wanted such a provision in the contract.

	“I told A24, ‘I don’t really know what the angle is, but there is something tickling in my brain,’” he said. “She was about to go to prison, so we didn’t know what was gonna happen. I was like, ‘If you guys want, I’m down to go down and start filming and see what emerges. But we need the ability to deliver nothing to you guys if it doesn’t work out.’ And they said ‘Sure.’”

	He continued: “It really meant I didn’t have to hold back with her or with them. Making a film, or any project, is very stressful. So if we had to pull the plug because it didn’t work out, it would sort of be a relief to me. It’s a very nice zone to operate in. Lance and I both thought, ‘Well, at the very least, this will be an interesting week or two that we’ll have as a story.’”

schema.headline: Nathan Fielder Negotiated a ‘Kill Switch’ on ‘You Can See Everything,’ Says Lance Oppenheim: ‘If We Didn’t Find Something, We Could Just Throw It All Away’

title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Star Anthony Ippolito on Becoming Sylvester Stallone and Acting With a Dog: ‘He Wasn’t a Huge Fan of Me’
description:
Anthony Ippolito had to do more than nail Sylvester Stallone’s signature voice to play him in “I Play Rocky.”

	He also had to transform his skinny
body:
Anthony Ippolito had to do more than nail Sylvester Stallone’s signature voice to play him in “I Play Rocky.”

	He also had to transform his skinny physique to one with bulging muscles.

	“It had its moments for sure. I was being tested,” Ippolito told me Saturday at the AFI Fest “I Play Rocky” screening in Los Angeles. “It’s like a consistency thing, though. I had a great deal of time, so just an entire lifestyle shift and it was just one of the priorities of every day for a pretty long period.”
	


	As Ippolito previously told Variety’s Clayton Davis, he spent nearly two years bulking up from about 150 pounds to roughly 180 while training at Gleason’s Gym in Brooklyn.


	What did family and friends think?

	“It happened over time, but a couple of people were like, ‘What’s going on?’” Ippolito recalled. “They didn’t necessarily know I was doing the prep, and they were like, ‘What’s going on here?’ I was like, ‘I’ve been going to the gym, been eating.’”

	“I Play Rocky,” directed by Peter Farrelly, follows Stallone’s journey to get “Rocky” made in 1976. Now considered one of the greatest films ever made, the odds were way more against Stallone than with him when he first pitched the movie in Hollywood.

	AnnaSophia Robb plays Stallone’s first wife, Sasha, in “I Play Rocky.” Stephan James portrays Carl Weathers. Rounding out the cast are Kiki Seto, P.J. Byrne, Matt Dillon, Tracy Letts and Jay Duplass.

	If jitters on the first day of filming weren’t already enough to contend with, Ippolito’s first scenes were with a dog playing Stallone’s pooch Butkus. Stallone famously sold Butkus for $40 when before he found fame because he couldn’t afford to feed him. After selling the “Rocky” script, he bought him back for $15,000.
	

Anthony Ippolito describes his first day filming "I Play Rocky": "Irwin Winkler was actually on set day one. We did a lot of stuff with Butkus that day, and I hadn't met that specific dog until the day prior to shooting, and he didn't happen to take a liking to me until a… pic.twitter.com/7tPKpNnp4M— Variety (@Variety) October 24, 2026


	“I hadn’t met that specific dog until like the day prior to shooting,” Ippolito said. “He didn’t happen to take a liking to me until a couple of days in. When you give him enough treats, then he started to warm up. But at that point he was, you know, a 140-, 160-pound dog [and] wasn’t a huge fan of me, so it kind of just added to it. He just did whatever he wanted to do, and that was usually not what we were looking for him to do … In some ways they, they give you the most beautiful stuff. It’s just you gotta be patient.”


	“I Play Rocky” is in limited release on Nov. 6, followed by going wide on Nov. 20.

	See more photos from the “I Play Rocky” screening at AFI Fest below.

									Variety via Getty Images
	





	

					Kiki Seto at the “I Play Rocky” Premiere during the AFI FEST 2026 held at TCL Chinese Theatre on October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Variety via Getty Images
	





	

					Peter Farrelly and Matt Dillon at the “I Play Rocky” Premiere during the AFI FEST 2026 held at TCL Chinese Theatre on October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Variety via Getty Images
	





	

					Stephan James at the “I Play Rocky” Premiere during the AFI FEST 2026 held at TCL Chinese Theatre on October 24, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. 
									Variety via Getty Images

title: Cynthia Erivo Plays Glinda in ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sketch on ‘SNL U.K.’: ‘She Wants a BBL That Defies Gravity’
description:
Cynthia Erivo spoofed “Wicked” during her stint hosting “SNL U.K.,” this time taking on the role of Glinda in “Nigerian Wicked.”

	Alongside Ayoade
body:
Cynthia Erivo spoofed “Wicked” during her stint hosting “SNL U.K.,” this time taking on the role of Glinda in “Nigerian Wicked.”

	Alongside Ayoade Bamgboye as Elphaba, Erivo — sporting a blonde wig and pink velour tracksuit — starred in a lo-fi, melodramatic version of the Oscar-nominated musical in which the two enemies-turned-friends go off to meet the Wizard of LagOz. 

	In “Wicked,” Erivo’s Elphaba and Ariana Grande’s Glinda express their frustration with each other in the song “What Is This Feeling.” But in “SNL U.K.’s” Nollywood version, Glinda simply slaps Elphaba across the face.
	

	“Glinda, you slapped me!” Bamgboye’s Elphaba says, to which Erivo’s Glinda replies: “Yes, because you are very classless.”


	The sketch also reimagines Glinda and Elphaba’s makeover scene, with Elphaba saying: “Glinda, I can’t afford this!” 

	“When we go to the Wizard, it will all pay off,” Erivo as Glinda replies.

	“The Wizard?” Bamgboye says. “But I’m a virgin!” The two then almost share a kiss, winking at fans who ship the characters together.

	When they finally make it to the “emerald, white and emerald city,” Erivo’s Glinda says she wants the Wizard to get her a Birkin bag, whereas Bamgboye’s Elphaba wants a “skinny BBL.”

	A voiceover from the Wizard himself, played by Hammed Animashaun, then rings out: “She wants a BBL that defies gravity!”

	But once they finally meet the Wizard, Glinda and Elphaba realize that he’s broke. “That’s a nolex,” Erivo’s Glinda says of his watch.

	Back at Shiz, Erivo’s Glinda asks Elphaba, “What do we do now?” The two then dramatically lean in for a kiss before an explosion effect engulfs the screen.
	

	“Nigerian Wicked: LGBTQ!” Animashaun’s voiceover concludes.

schema.headline: Cynthia Erivo Plays Glinda in ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sketch on ‘SNL U.K.’: ‘She Wants a BBL That Defies Gravity’

title: ‘SNL U.K.’ Weekend Update Tackles Meghan Markle Dad Allegations, James Bond Auditions and ‘Glee’ Reboot
description: “Saturday Night Live U.K.’s” Weekend Update isn’t afraid to tackle the most controversial topics, as the show proved again this weekend when co-hos
body:
“Saturday Night Live U.K.’s” Weekend Update isn’t afraid to tackle the most controversial topics, as the show proved again this weekend when co-host Paddy Young directly referenced the allegations that emerged this past week regarding Meghan Markle’s father.

	“In royal news, it’s been a big 24 hours for Meghan Markle, whose dad has been accused of being an alleged pedophile, in another pathetic attempt to win over the British public,” he said.
	

	“In 2025, Thomas Markle moved to the Philippines in a sure sign of his innocence. If the allegations about Meghan Markle’s father are true and he is a pedophile, there is a genuine chance Meghan could be considered royal.”


	That wasn’t the only provocative subject that came up during the latest Weekend Update. Young’s fellow host Ania Magliano also brought up the recently-announced “Glee” reboot – taking a shot squarely at the show itself.

	“This week, it was announced that the musical comedy ‘Glee’ will be rebooted on Disney+,” said Magliano. “The original series was famously struck by repeated tragedies, including multiple cast deaths, and also being written, produced, and broadcast.”

	Young also threw his hat in the ring for the James Bond auditions, which are said to be taking place this weekend, telling the audience: “I know this is late, but I’d like to put myself forward.” He immediately (purposely) fluffed it, bluring out: “The James Bond — bollocks.”

	And he also threw in a shot at the BBC, saying: “In big media news, Radio Four Extra has announced it will close in what is sure to be devastating news for its listener.”

schema.headline: ‘SNL U.K.’ Weekend Update Tackles Meghan Markle Dad Allegations, James Bond Auditions and ‘Glee’ Reboot

title: Shia LaBeouf Would Trash-Talk ‘Lizzie McGuire’ While Filming ‘Even Stevens,’ Says Christy Carlson Romano: ‘He Wanted to Be the Number One Show’
description: Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the sitcom “Even Stevens,” has revealed that co-star Shia LaBeouf used to trash-talk competing Disne
body:
Christy Carlson Romano, who first broke out on the sitcom “Even Stevens,” has revealed that co-star Shia LaBeouf used to trash-talk competing Disney Channel show “Lizzie McGuire” and that he was “definitely beefing” with the show’s star, Hilary Duff.

	“Hilary had no clue about that. I’m sure she was doing her own thing, but he would always be kind of like trash-talking ‘Lizzie McGuire,’” Romano said on a recent episode of “The Joe Vulpis Podcast.” “I was always like, ‘We don’t know anything about them. Like why are you…’” she recalled, adding that he was “very competitive.”
	

	She continued: “He wanted to be the number one show on the network. He had to be the number one show because I think his life depended on that show doing well… He had a rough upbringing, and I think he needed that show to do well for him.” Earlier in the episode, the actress explained that while the actors didn’t have “beef” with rival actors at Nickelodeon, there was competition within the network to get the best ratings.


	Last month, ahead of the release of her memoir, “Once Upon a Trainwreck: The Fall and Rise of a Child Star,” Romano said that she and LaBeouf were “like oil and water” while guesting on a podcast, despite being just 14 and 12 years old, respectively, at the time.

	Romano explained that their on-set incompatibility stemmed from how they were raised.

	“I was being raised and brought up to be this type A, I mean exactly like Ren Stevens. Like, you know your lines, you hit your marks, you don’t mess up,” she said. “You’re a New York kid, like that comes with a certain echelon… I was trying to go to pre-college Juilliard… everything we were doing, my mom called it cross-training, came with a certain dollar amount of training.”
	

	In comparison, LaBeouf has long been open about his tumultuous childhood and has said that his father was a recovering addict, and at times abusive. “He was a Venice Beach kind of bum kid,” said Romano. “It’s like that kind of vagrant fun, but also very chaotic and very scary lifestyle, and he was very young to be having that.” She likened his upbringing to the lifestyle depicted in the 1995 Larry Clark film “Kids.”

	Romano later starred alongside Duff in the Disney Channel original movie “Cadet Kelly.”

schema.headline: Shia LaBeouf Would Trash-Talk ‘Lizzie McGuire’ While Filming ‘Even Stevens,’ Says Christy Carlson Romano: ‘He Wanted to Be the Number One Show’

body:
Kristi Noem
                          Accused of Creating Fake Press Release After Exiting Latest Job
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Kristi Noem allegedly created a fake press release using doctored State Department letterhead to explain why she was exiting her special envoy role after getting fired as DHS secretary ... this according to reports.
      
    
            After the State Department announced her exit, Noem shared a press release on State Department letterhead, saying ... "The Special Envoy to the Shield of the Americas role was always a six-month appointment. Secretary Noem remains at the State Department as a Senior Advisor."
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            The issue? Sources at the State Department say it was not an official release ... and that the letterhead was fabricated.
      

            A person familiar with the situation told Politico ... "This was not a press release put out by the State Department. Noem went rogue and created a fake letterhead to post on X."
      
    
        Waiting for your permission to load the Twitter Tweet.
      
    
            An official confirmed the same to CBS News' Olivia Gazis ... who wrote ... "A State Department official confirmed that a statement posted by Kristi Noem to her official envoy account and personal X account was created using fabricated State Department letterhead and was not an official department press release."
      
    
                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            We've reached out to the State Department and Kristi for comment ... so far, no word back.

title: Six Flags Over Georgia's Goliath Roller Coaster Getting Seat Belts, Will Reopen
description:
Six Flags Over Georgia
                          Goliath Roller Coaster To Reopen With Seat Belts
body:
Six Flags Over Georgia
                          Goliath Roller Coaster To Reopen With Seat Belts
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Six Flags Over Georgia's Goliath roller coaster is set to be reopened with new safety features once the ride has been retrofitted ... after a man was violently thrown to his death earlier this month.
      
    
            The theme park announced seat belts would be added to the ride ... as well as other rides with similar restraints ... CEO John Reilly revealed in a statement Friday.
      
    
            Reilly added ... "Goliath at Six Flags Over Georgia remains closed pending necessary safety reviews and clearances. Eight additional rides at five other parks are temporarily closed out of an abundance of caution. Our parks remain open, including throughout Halloween weekend, with more than 220 roller coasters operating across our parks."
      

            We reported earlier ... Hassan Kariem died after he became unrestrained during the ride, flew off the coaster and struck the tracks multiple times.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            In the wake of his death ... parks across the country temporarily halted operations on several high-speed coasters with similar lap bar restraints.
      
    
            Kariem's family told us that he was laid to rest earlier this week.
      
    
            The educator was only 42.
      
    
            RIP

title: 'The Challenge' Star Anika Rashaun Dead at 34
description:
'The Challenge' Star
                          Anika Rashaun Dead at 34 From Breast Cancer
body:
'The Challenge' Star
                          Anika Rashaun Dead at 34 From Breast Cancer
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Anika Rashaun -- who starred on hit reality shows like "The Challenge" and "The Real World" -- has died from breast cancer ... her friends have revealed.
      
    
            The TV star-turned-dating coach died on Oct. 1 after being diagnosed with cancer last summer.
      
    
            Cyndi Rich wrote on Facebook ... "Anika shined so bright. Being close to that light as one of her closest friends was a true blessing. She is a vibrant soul. I’ll love her and treasure the 16 years of memories forever."
      

            Another friend Tiara Ramos wrote on Substack ... "Anika Rashaun Walker Rehn was part of my life longer than she wasn’t. She was my mirror: the good, the bad, the ugly, the really ugly. She wasn’t just my friend. She was my other half. If you knew me, you knew her."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Tiara also wrote that despite the fact her mother had breast cancer years earlier ... "she was never identified as high-risk or told by her doctors to prioritize mammograms."
      
    
            She added ... "That was one of the many failures she experienced within the medical system during her time battling cancer."
      
    
            Anika -- who previously appeared on "The Real World" 2016-2017 "Bad Blood" season and on "The Challenge: Invasion of the Champions" in 2017 -- was 34.
      
    
            RIP

Bhad Bhabie
                          Cash Me Out of My Florida Mansion!!!
                          $6.9M Estate Hits Market
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                October 24, 2026
                
                            10:23 AM PDT

                                12:30 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
            Bhad Bhabie is looking to unload her massive Florida mansion ... and she's hoping to pocket nearly $7 million in the process ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Real estate sources tell TMZ ... the rapper's Boca Raton estate hit the market Wednesday with an asking price of $6.9 million.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The sprawling 8,958-square-foot property boasts 7 bedrooms and 7 bathrooms, sitting on a beautifully landscaped acre in an exclusive guard-gated community.
      

                    
                          
                                  
      
        
    
            BB purchased the mansion for $6.1 million back in March 2022 ... meaning she's looking to sell it for $800K more than she paid.
      
    
            Inside, the mansion features a gourmet kitchen with oversized islands, expansive living spaces, a private office, billiards room, wine storage, and even a dry sauna.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The first floor primary suite is especially impressive ... featuring a spa-like bathroom, private outdoor Jacuzzi and not one, not two, but THREE massive custom walk-in closets.
      
    
            And there's plenty of room for company ... with a separate 2-story guest house featuring its own kitchen and living accommodations.
      
    
            Outside, the property feels more like a private resort, complete with a massive swimming pool, spa, lush tropical landscaping, and plenty of space for entertaining.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            There's also a 6-car garage ... perfect for showing off a serious car collection.
      
    
            Marcy F. Javor of Signature One Luxury Estates LLC holds the listing.

body:
Prostitution Scam Case
                          Teacher Accused of Holding Naked Man Down, Sending $1K in Apple Pay: Report
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A New Jersey middle school teacher has been accused of running a prostitution scam that involved her allegedly pinning down a naked man ... but she claims she was "strictly there to party."
      
    
            An unidentified man claims he met Middle Township Middle School computer teacher Amanda Crafts, 35, and Veda Engel, 23, at Caesar’s Atlantic City on Oct. 9 ... the New York Post reported.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The victim claims that after Engel performed a sex act on him in the women's Harrah's hotel room ... Crafts held him down and used his smartphone's Face ID to open up Apple Pay to send 4 separate payments totaling $1,250.
      

            Craft's legal team has denied her involvement in pinning the man down ... and rejected the claim that she knew Engel was a prostitute.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Crafts' attorney told the NYP ... "Amanda Crafts is highly intelligent and wouldn’t participate in anything like that. She was in the room and wanted to leave and didn’t even realize it was a prostitution thing. She is mortified."
      
    
            Since her arrest on Oct. 9 and release on Oct. 15 ... Crafts is out of a job.
      
    
            Middle Township Middle School announced in a letter on Oct. 19 to parents and fellow staffers that she was "no longer employed by the district."
      
    
            Craft faces 2 charges connected to the alleged prostitution scam.
